one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is the fiscal Q1 FY27 report. The quarter closed 2026-10-02. No date had been announced as of 2026-10-02 (a search found no announcement), but the last three Q1 reports came on 2023-10-26, 2024-10-22 and 2025-10-28, so the report is very likely (~90%) before Nov 1. Guidance is $4.1B +/- $0.1B revenue and $7.30 +/- $0.20 non-GAAP EPS at a ~50% op margin. Q4 FY26 beat, and the CFO said September pricing was helped by demand and 'a little bit more pricing benefit', so a beat and a higher Q2 guide are likely. The reaction depends on what management says about CY2028 pricing and Toshiba. Pricing is contracted only through CY2027, so a vague answer could cap any rebound. The July print showed how two-sided these reactions can be (-8.5% on the day, then +14% over the next two days). I add only a small drift for the likely beat and the partial reversal of the sentiment-driven 11% drop on 2026-10-02. I set the median at about $842 with a monthly sigma of about 20.5% (75%/3.5 is about 21%). P(close >= 837.52) = 0.51, close to neutral on purpose and a point below round 1.

fair_value.method: Forward P/E: probability-weighted NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $47.5 (flat CY2028 pricing ~$41 at 30%, modest +5-10% ~$48 at 50%, strong ~$56 at 20%) x 17 = $808, weight 0.6. FCF yield: $40.8 FCF per share (86% conversion of $47.5 EPS on 230M shares) at 5% = $816, plus ~$8 per share of net cash by the horizon = $824, weight 0.4. Blend is about $815.

inputs_detail.input: NTM EPS at horizon, CY2028 pricing cases
inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 call: 'the vast majority of our nearline exabytes are now allocated into calendar 2028', but contracts with set pricing cover only CY2027. So CY2028 price per EB is still being negotiated, while Toshiba's capacity add lands around April 2027 to March 2028 (Investing.com/Nikkei). From a Q4 FY27 run-rate of about $9.8 and flat units with mid-20s exabyte growth: flat price/EB means cost-per-TB gains only, about $10.2 per quarter (~$41). Modest pricing gives about $12. Strong (Toshiba limited by outside heads/media, demand above supply) gives about $14. I give the flat case 30% because Toshiba's plan is credible but limited by components and by being MAMR-only until FY2028.

About 24x FY27 today ($838 / ~$34-36). HDD peak-cycle history is 8-15x, and STX fell 44% in 2018 and 60% in 2022 after cycle peaks (supervisor check). I use 17x for the 2028 volume visibility and the 90% data-center mix, discounted because the horizon multiple will price an earnings peak.

226.8M basic at 2026-07-03 (10-K) plus 1,647,862 shares issued on the exchangeable settlement on 2026-09-08 (8-K) = about 228.6M basic. The 231M Q1 guide included ~2M of convert dilution, which has now ended. I hold 230M for RSU dilution and assume buybacks offset it, which is conservative.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 conversion was about 0.87. The working-capital build as revenue grows and the higher cash taxes on a 16% rate keep it a little lower. Tied to EPS rather than a revenue margin, so the FCF leg cannot be more aggressive than the P/E leg.

inputs_detail.input: Net debt now and at horizon
inputs_detail.value: Gross debt ~$2.4B after the Sep quarter (from $3.6B at 2026-07-03); net debt ~$0.5-0.7B today; ~+$1.8B net cash (~$8/share) by Oct-2027
inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 call: gross debt was about $3.6B at fiscal year end and 'we are retiring an additional $1.2 billion' in the September quarter, which includes the exchangeables settled 2026-09-08 (8-K). Cash was $1.7B at FYE, less about $1.2B of retirements plus about $1.5B of Q1 FCF, less dividends, leaves about $1.8B, so net debt is about $0.6B. FY27 FCF of about $7B less ~$0.7B of dividends and assumed heavy buybacks from the $4.8B authorization gives about +$1.8B of net cash at the horizon.
A peak-cycle risk premium and 14% single-customer concentration (10-K) call for a yield above today's implied ~4% on FY27.

bear.story: CY2028 LTA negotiations come in at flat-to-down price per EB as Toshiba's MAMR capacity and WDC additions arrive, and a hyperscaler capex pause or BTO deferral follows. NTM EPS slides toward about $40, and the market pays a peak-cycle ~10-11x. That is consistent with the -44% (2018) and -60% (2022) post-peak drawdowns.

base.story: FY27 is delivered as guided (sequential growth, EPS about $34), and CY2028 contracts settle at modest mid-single-digit price/EB increases. NTM EPS is about $48. The multiple compresses from ~24x to ~17x, and with about $8 per share of net cash the price ends roughly flat.

bull.story: Toshiba's expansion is limited by outside head and media supply and MAMR-only products, AI inference/KV-cache demand keeps exabytes short, CY2028 pricing rises 10-15%, and LTAs extend into 2029. NTM EPS is $56+ at about 22-23x.

thesis_break_reason: About $520 (-38%) is about 11x the probability-weighted NTM EPS of $47.5 and about 12.7x the flat-pricing case of $41, close to the HDD peak-cycle multiple. Trading there would mean the market is pricing an actual break: CY2028 LTA pricing flat to down with volumes slipping too, a hyperscaler deferring or cancelling BTO volumes, or a Mozaic 4/5 yield or qualification slip. That would be a fundamental change, not 75%-vol noise; 2026's one-day sector shocks bottomed around $700-750.

reasoning: Round 2 changes the evidence base, not the structure. (1) The supervisor showed that the $55.37 FY28 'consensus' I anchored on rests on one 24/7 Wall St article with no named provider and an inconsistent forward-EPS figure. Alpha Vantage and Twelve Data estimate endpoints were unavailable, so I could not verify it. I dropped it as an anchor and built NTM EPS from primary guidance plus explicit CY2028 pricing cases. (2) Re-reading the Q4 FY26 transcript confirms that volume is allocated into CY2028 but contracted pricing covers only CY2027. When asked about outer-year pricing visibility, the CEO spoke about unit and component strategy, not price, so I give a flat-pricing CY2028 case (~$41 NTM) 30% weight. (3) The September-quarter jump in price per EB was helped by a preferential-price HAMR customer rolling off. The CFO says that effect was 'minimal' and that demand drove most of it, so I keep FY27 sequential growth but do not extrapolate 20%+ pricing. On (3) I partly disagree with the supervisor: the call says the roll-off was minor, so it does not by itself argue for lower FY27 numbers. (4) My debt and share-count facts were confirmed: gross debt is about $2.4B, net debt about $0.6B today, net cash about +$1.8B (~$8/share) at the horizon, and about 230M diluted shares. (5) I tied FCF to 86% of EPS instead of a 45% revenue margin, which removed the round-1 inconsistency. The result is NTM EPS of $47.5 x 17 = $808 and FCF of $40.8/sh at 5% + $8 net cash = $824, a blend of about $815 (from $845). That is slightly below spot and slightly above the supervisor's $805, the difference being mainly the net cash I credit. Scenario mean is about $852 (25% $430 / 50% $830 / 25% $1,320) and the median about $825. For the ladder I use a lognormal around the $825 median at an effective vol of about 62-68%, below the realized 75% because FY27 is contracted, but with the left tail kept fat for the -44%/-60% post-peak base rates. The at-the-money probability falls from 0.505 to 0.49, as the supervisor's revisit suggested. The 52-week low is about $212 (Oct 14, 2025 close), not $209. Research this round was limited: two data APIs blocked, one search and one primary transcript re-read.
